learn.title: From flat to solid
learn.body: Volume measures the space inside a solid, in cubic units. A prism has two identical parallel faces, the bases, joined by flat sides. A cylinder is similar, with circles as bases. For both, the volume formula follows one idea.

learn.title: Base times height
learn.body: Imagine stacking layers, each the same shape as the base. The volume is the area of the base $B$ times the height $h$: $V=Bh$. For a box, $B=lw$. For a cylinder, $B=\pi r^2$, so $V=\pi r^2h$.

learn.title: Compute volumes
steps: Triangular prism with a triangle of base 6 and height 4, length 10: $B=12$, $V=120$.

learn.body: The height of a prism is the distance between the two bases, not the length of a slanted edge.

questions.prompt: Find the volume of a box that is 4 by 3 by 5.
What is the volume formula for any prism?
questions.explanation: Base area times height. The one-half belongs to pyramids and triangles.

questions.prompt: A triangular prism has a triangle base of base 6 and height 4, and length 10. Find its volume.
A cylinder has radius 3 and height 10. What is its volume in terms of $\pi$?
A cube has side 4. Find its volume.
A cylinder's radius doubles and its height stays the same. What happens to the volume?
questions.explanation: Volume depends on $r^2$, so doubling $r$ makes it 4 times larger.

questions.prompt: A box has a square base of side 5 and volume 150. Find its height.
